topics.name: Polite words (please, may I, could you, thank you)

questions.rule: An instruction starts with the base form of the verb: Look at the speaker.
With one person (he/she/a listener), the present verb takes -s: pays.
Wh-word + does + subject + base verb: What does this word mean?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Listeners is plural, so the verb has no -s: pay.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Instructions use the base form of the verb: Please sit ... and listen.
We ask for permission politely with May I ...?
Where asks about a place.
Please + base verb makes a polite instruction: Please close the door.

chat: Here is the pencil you asked for.
questions.rule: Say Thank you or Thanks, but never 'Thanks you'.

chat: Does your brother play the flute?
options: Yes, he play it every evening.
Yes, he plays it every evening.
Yes, he playing it every evening.
questions.rule: For a habit, use the simple present; with he, add -s: he plays.

options: Don't talk while others are speaking.
Not talk while others are speaking.
Don't talks while others are speaking.
questions.rule: A 'do not' instruction is Don't + base verb: Don't talk.

options: Where do the speaker come from?
Where does the speaker come from?
Where does the speaker comes from?
questions.rule: One speaker takes does, and after does the verb has no -s: come.

options: Could you speaks a little louder, please?
Could you speak a little louder, please?
Could you spoke a little louder, please?
questions.rule: After Could you, use the base form of the verb: speak.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Grandma is one person (her book) and every night shows a habit: tells.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After does, use the base form of the verb: does the baby cry?

questions.after: down the important points as you listen.
questions.rule: An instruction begins with the base verb: Note down the points.
The teacher is one person, so the present verb takes -s: speaks.
Wh-word + is + subject + -ing verb: What is the speaker saying?

chat: I heard a strange sound outside.
options: What kind of sound you heard?
What kind of sound did you heard?
What kind of sound did you hear?
questions.rule: Past questions use did + base verb: did you hear?

chat: There is water on the floor.
questions.rule: Instructions use the base form: be careful, Don't slip.

options: She do not understand the new word.
She does not understand the new word.
She does not understands the new word.
questions.rule: With she, use does not + base verb: does not understand.

options: How often does you listen to the radio?
How often you listen to the radio?
How often do you listen to the radio?
questions.rule: With you, the helper is do, and it comes before the subject.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After May I, use the base form of the verb: May I borrow?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Two instructions joined by and both use the base verb: Listen ... and wait.

questions.after: pen is this? Is it yours?
questions.rule: Whose asks who something belongs to. Who's means 'who is'.

questions.after: you please pass me the salt?
questions.rule: A polite request begins with Could you please + base verb?
May I + base verb asks for permission politely.
A plural subject (listeners) takes the verb without -s: look.

options: No, she don't like it at all.
No, she doesn't likes it at all.
No, she doesn't like it at all.
questions.rule: With she, use doesn't + base verb: she doesn't like.

options: I would like two pens, please.
I would likes two pens, please.
I would like two pen, please.
questions.rule: After would, use the base verb like; two needs the plural pens.

options: What did the teacher say in the assembly?
What did the teacher said in the assembly?
What the teacher said in the assembly?
questions.rule: Past questions use did + base verb: What did the teacher say?

options: Bring me the vase that have pink roses.
Bring me the vase that has pink roses.
Brings me the vase that has pink roses.
questions.rule: Instructions start with the base verb Bring; one vase has roses.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Two cousins is plural, so the verb has no -s: live ... and visit.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Both your brothers is plural, so the question uses were.

questions.after: Arjun always sit in the front row?
questions.rule: One person (Arjun) takes does + base verb: Why does Arjun sit ...?

questions.after: afraid to ask questions in class.
questions.rule: afraid is not a verb, so the instruction needs be: Don't be afraid.
Wh-word + did + subject + base verb: Where did you find ...?
Please don't + base verb makes a polite 'do not' instruction.
Mrs Joshi is one person, so the present verb takes -es: teaches.

chat: Can someone help me carry these books?
questions.rule: To offer help, say I will help you: will + base verb.

options: Do you know what will the speaker say next?
Do you know what the speaker will says next?
Do you know what the speaker will say next?
questions.rule: Inside a longer question, keep normal order: what the speaker will say.

options: Each of the students look at the speaker when she talks.
Each of the students looks at the speaker when she talks.
Each of the students looks at the speaker when she talk.
questions.rule: Each means every single one, so the verb is singular: looks; she talks.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Ms Rao is one person, so use is speaking.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After does, the main verb is in the base form: does Kavya learn?

questions.after: you tell me the way to the post office?
questions.rule: Ask a stranger politely with Could you + base verb.

questions.after: to note down important points while you listen.
questions.rule: It takes a verb with -s in the simple present: it helps.
Start with the base verb Wait; to finish tells what the speaker must do.
Which + noun + do you + base verb: Which sounds do you like?

chat: Good morning, Sunshine Clinic. How may I help you?
options: Good morning. May I speaks to Dr Mehta, please?
Good morning. May I to speak to Dr Mehta, please?
Good morning. May I speak to Dr Mehta, please?
questions.rule: May I is followed directly by the base verb: May I speak?

chat: I can't hear the teacher from the back.
options: Then comes and sit in the front row with me.
Then come and sitting in the front row with me.
Then come and sit in the front row with me.
questions.rule: Both instructions use the base verb: come and sit.
